q: Restriction enzymes act on DNA by:
o: Cutting DNA at specific recognition sequences
why: Restriction endonucleases recognize and cut specific DNA sequences, creating sticky ends.

q: Which of the following is a commonly used restriction enzyme?
why: EcoRI is a widely used restriction enzyme in recombinant DNA technology.

q: A vector used in genetic engineering must be able to:
o: Replicate independently inside the host and carry a marker gene
why: A good vector self-replicates in the host and has a selectable marker gene.

q: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is primarily used to:
o: Amplify a specific DNA segment into many copies
why: PCR exponentially amplifies a target DNA sequence using repeated cycles.

q: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments mainly based on their:
o: Size (and charge), smaller fragments move farther
why: In an electric field, smaller DNA fragments move faster through the gel matrix.

q: Bt cotton is genetically modified to resist:
why: Bt cotton expresses a toxin gene from Bacillus thuringiensis that kills bollworm larvae.

q: Gene therapy aims to treat genetic disorders by:
o: Removing all genes from a cell
Inserting a correct/functional gene to replace a defective one
why: Gene therapy corrects genetic disease by introducing a normal copy of the defective gene.

q: If two sticky ends are to join successfully, the DNA fragments must have been cut by:
why: Identical restriction enzymes produce complementary sticky ends that can base-pair and join.

q: The first step of recombinant DNA technology typically involves:
o: Inserting the gene directly into the organism's body
Isolating the desired gene and the vector DNA
why: Recombinant DNA technology begins with isolation of the gene of interest and a suitable vector.

q: GM crops like Bt cotton are called 'genetically modified' because they contain:
o: A foreign gene inserted from another organism
why: GM crops carry a gene transferred from a different organism, giving a new trait.
